A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAMMs research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original change-description and image-forecasting results in Table 1, component ablations in Table 2, qualitative predictions, and appendix analyses of description length and training losses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a prompt robustness experiment in Appendix A.5 and Table 3.

M1.justification: The PTE, CTP and SFCI components, frozen backbones, losses and staged training procedure remain unchanged. The default prompt is identical. Additional backbone information and tested prompt variants do not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same change-description and forecasting tasks, 37,003 fMoW training sequences across 58 categories, and 150 Google Earth test sequences. The prompt variants and added caption examples introduce no additional dataset, domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Section 4.2.1, Table 1 and the description-length analysis are unchanged. v3 newly mentions preliminary experiments with Chameleon and Janus-Pro against unspecified specialized models, leaving unclear whether either was actually evaluated against TAMMs.

E3.justification: Appendix A.5 introduces an evaluation varying instruction detail across short, default and verbose prompts, assessed with TCS, BLEU-4 and CIDEr-D. Existing data splits, sequence lengths, benchmark metrics and training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a targeted sensitivity analysis testing whether CTP performance depends on prompt detail. The existing component ablations, generated-description length analysis and training-loss analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. v3's statement that TCS fluctuates by less than 0.015 describes differences across prompt settings, not uncertainty estimated from repeated runs.

E6.justification: The benchmark, component-ablation and description-length values are unchanged. New Table 3 reports short/default/verbose prompt results: TCS 0.9580/0.9690/0.9615, BLEU-4 0.2610/0.2669/0.2675 and CIDEr-D 0.8910/0.9030/0.8980. v3 also adds a qualitative report of preliminary Chameleon and Janus-Pro performance shortcomings without numerical comparisons.

T1.justification: The task definitions, TCS formulation in Equations 1–3, PTE/SFCI mathematics in Equations 4–8, and appendix training losses in Equations 9–10 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about unified change understanding and forecasting, TAM, SFCI, TCS and superiority over specialist baselines. The revised title and introductory wording do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds an interpretation prioritizing perceptual and temporal fidelity over distortion metrics, explains backbone selection and rejection of native unified alternatives, and interprets prompt robustness as evidence that learnable visual alignment dominates prompt wording. Existing future-work qualifications about long horizons, abrupt events and uncertainty remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly identifies the DiffusionSat backbone's Stable Diffusion 2-1 basis, supplies the additional robustness prompts, and illustrates Qwen2.5-VL scene captions. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, training schedules and access statements are retained; these additions mainly improve documentation.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chameleon and Janus-Pro references and a limited discussion positioning its architecture against native unified multimodal models. The main related-work sections and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title, affiliations and conference header, lightly edits the introduction, expands selected discussions, and adds acknowledgements and small appendix subsections. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains colored PTE/CTP/SFCI boundaries and a revised scene-description icon. v3 adds prompt-results Table 3 and caption-example Figure 7, relocates Figure 6, and reflows and renumbers retained appendix displays. Existing benchmark illustrations and plots remain.

improvement.justification: The new prompt experiment supplies limited robustness evidence absent from v2, while exact prompt variants, clearer module annotations and caption examples improve transparency. The main findings remain unchanged. The preliminary unified-model comparison lacks concrete supporting results, and prompt stability does not establish visual alignment's causal primacy, so the overall gain is useful but modest.
